title: One God and Six Beliefs
objective: After this level you can explain tawhid, the oneness of God, and the six articles of faith that Muslims hold.
summary: Tawhid, the oneness of God, is the root of Muslim belief; from it grow six articles of faith: God, angels, holy books, prophets, the Day of Judgement and God's decree.

cards.headline: Islam's creed begins with a no.
cards.body: "There is no god but God, and Muhammad is his messenger." Before it tells you what to believe, it clears the field. That testimony expresses tawhid, and everything in this level grows from it.

cards.headline: Tawhid: God is one
cards.body: Tawhid means "making one" or "asserting oneness". Muslims believe God is a unity, not made of parts, with no children, no parents and no partners, and no shape or form that can be seen. Its opposite is shirk, associating anything else with God. In Muslim teaching it is the one sin God will not forgive in the hereafter.

cards.headline: Allah: the Arabic word for God
cards.body: Allah is the standard Arabic word for God, probably a contraction of al-Ilah, "the God". It isn't a word only Muslims use: Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews say Allah too. So when you hear a Muslim say Allah, you can simply hear "God".

cards.headline: Six articles of faith
cards.body: From tawhid grow six main beliefs that Muslims hold. God is one. Angels exist, even if people cannot see them. God revealed holy books. God sent prophets, from Adam and Abraham to Moses and Jesus, with Muhammad the last. A Day of Judgement will come. And God knows all that will happen, which Muslims believe does not stop people from choosing freely.
cards.callout: God, angels, books, prophets, Judgement Day, God's decree

cards.headline: Shared beliefs, many voices
cards.body: How widely are these beliefs held? In Pew surveys of Muslims in 39 countries, belief in one God and in Muhammad as his Prophet was nearly unanimous in most. Belief in fate varied far more: under half in Albania, over nine in ten in Azerbaijan and Turkey. That's Level 4 again: no faith speaks with a single voice.

cards.headline: One God and Six Beliefs: the takeaways
learned: Tawhid means God is one, with no partners
Allah is the Arabic word for God, used by Christians and Jews too
Muslims hold six articles of faith, from angels to God's decree

questions.prompt: One of the six articles of faith that Muslims hold is belief in _____.

options.label: the hijra
options.rationale: The hijra is an event, not an article of faith.

options.label: the caliphs
options.rationale: Caliphs were leaders, not an article of faith.

options.label: the Arabic alphabet
options.rationale: Not on the list of six.

questions.explanation: The six: God, angels, holy books, prophets, the Day of Judgement and God's decree.

questions.prompt: Match each Islamic word about God with its meaning.
questions.explanation: Tawhid means asserting God's oneness, shirk is associating anything else with God, and Allah is the Arabic word for God.

questions.prompt: An Arabic-speaking Christian, from another of Level 8's Abrahamic faiths, prays to Allah. Why is that unsurprising?

options.label: Allah is simply the Arabic word for God
Christians borrowed the word from the Quran
options.rationale: It's the ordinary Arabic word for God, not a borrowing.

options.label: Allah is the name of a prophet
options.rationale: Allah means God, not a prophet.

options.label: Arab Christians share the Muslim creed
options.rationale: Using the Arabic word for God doesn't mean sharing the creed.

questions.explanation: Allah is the standard Arabic word for God, used by Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews as well as Muslims.
